findings.reason: Diff hook runs `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD` in process.cwd() and exits 0 for main/master. dev-team-process.md:55 requires implementers to use `isolation: "worktree"`, so the lead's checkout is not the implementer's branch. A lead on main sending shutdown_request to voss-implement-773 is always allowed.
findings.claim: The guard reads the branch from the sender's (team lead's) checkout, not the target implementer's, so a lead on main/master always gets an allow.
findings.evidence: Line 82 runs `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD` in process.cwd(), and line 91 exits 0 when that branch is `main`/`master`. Implementers in team mode must use `isolation: "worktree"` (templates/dev-team-process.md:55), and their worktree is removed after the PR is created (templates/skills/dev-team-implement/SKILL.md:86), so the lead's checkout is not on the implementer's branch. Trigger: a lead on `main` sends `{to:"voss-implement-773", message:{type:"shutdown_request"}}`. The hook gets past the tool-name, shutdown and target checks, then hits `branch === "main"` at line 91 and exits 0. If the lead is on some other feature branch, every implementer is judged against that branch's sidecars. The `.reviews` lookup at line 97 also uses the lead's cwd. The tests hide this: beforeEach puts the hook's own cwd on the implementer's branch `feat/123-test`.

findings.reason: ADR-029:48 fixes sidecar names as `<agent>--<file-content-hash>.json`, and review-gate.js:140/152 builds exactly that name. The guard only tests `f.includes(sanitizedBranch)` and never reads the `branch` field the way merge-gate.js:153-154 does, so real sidecars never match and shutdown stays blocked. The passing test uses a made-up name, `knuth--feat-123-test.json`.
findings.claim: Review evidence is matched only by the branch name in the sidecar filename, but real sidecars are named `<agent>--<content-hash>.json`, so real review evidence never counts.
findings.evidence: Line 103: `files.some((f) => f.includes(sanitizedBranch) && f.endsWith(".json"))`. The file content is never read. ADR-029 (docs/adr/029-stateless-commit-gates.md:48) fixes sidecar names as `.dev-team/.reviews/<agent>--<file-content-hash>.json`, and review-gate.js:140 only accepts names ending `--${contentHash}.json`. The existing merge gate matches on the sidecar's `branch` JSON field first (merge-gate.js:153-154). Trigger: `.dev-team/.reviews/szabo--a1b2c3d4e5f6.json` containing `{"branch":"feat/123-test"}` passes the merge gate, but the guard finds no `feat-123-test` in the filename and exits 2. The passing test only works because it invents the filename `knuth--feat-123-test.json` (tests/unit/hooks.test.js:2864).

findings.reason: The guard sets hasReviewEvidence from filenames alone and exits 0. No sidecar content (findings/resolved) is ever read. The file header and dev-team-task SKILL.md:80 both say implementers stay alive until findings are routed and acknowledged.
findings.claim: Shutdown is allowed once any matching sidecar exists, even with unresolved [DEFECT] findings, so 'until findings are routed and acknowledged' is not enforced.
findings.evidence: Lines 102-112 only test that a matching filename exists, then `if (hasReviewEvidence) process.exit(0)`. Neither `findings` nor `resolved` is ever read. The header (lines 5-10) says it blocks agents 'that have open, unreviewed PRs' until 'all review findings have been routed and acknowledged'. README.md:153 says 'before review findings are routed', and templates/skills/dev-team-task/SKILL.md:80 sets the routed-and-acknowledged rule. review-gate.js:262 shows the existing pattern: it checks `finding.classification === "[DEFECT]" && !finding.resolved`. Trigger: a reviewer writes a sidecar whose name matches the branch, with `findings:[{classification:"[DEFECT]",resolved:false}]`. The guard exits 0, which is the moment findings are about to be routed to the implementer.

findings.reason: init.ts:23/30 does allow `review: "complex"`, and the guard disables itself only on `=== false`. But nothing in the repo defines what review "complex" means (only challenge "complex" is documented at init.ts:84), so the trigger isn't shown. Lowered from medium to low.
findings.claim: `workflow.review: "complex"` is treated as review always on, which may block shutdown on SIMPLE tasks.
findings.evidence: src/init.ts:23 and :30 type `review` as `WorkflowToggle = boolean | "complex"`, but the guard only disables itself when `config.workflow.review === false` (line 69). If `"complex"` means review only for COMPLEX tasks, which is how the `challenge: "complex"` toggle reads in init.ts:84-88, a SIMPLE task leaves no sidecar and the guard reaches exit 2 at line 120. No test covers the `"complex"` value.
